evidence.domain: Compared against Bradley-Terry/Thurstone paired-comparison practice and Glickman 2012. Sound: Glicko-2 matches the paper to full double precision on single-game periods in five new cases; per-respondent state; DerSimonian-Laird random-effects pooling (Biostatistics standard); Davidson ties. Departures a psychometrician flags, unchanged: (1) Glicko-2 is an order-dependent online rating, while a Bradley-Terry fit on all of a respondent's answers is the usual order-invariant survey estimator; (2) a Glicko RD is a posterior spread, not a sampling standard error, so DL pooling of RDs labelled a '95% interval' is a heuristic and the docs do not say so beside the number; (3) MIN_RD 30 and a normal quantile with 2 to 3 raters can make intervals look tighter than the data justify; (4) the 'trade-offs they couldn't state' claim rests on a ridge-prior conjoint model whose identifiability with 10 to 20 answers is simulated, not validated on humans.

defects.what: Pooled 95% intervals and tau are unpinned by tests: Z95 1.96 to 1.64 and the DL numerator (q-(k-1)) to (q-k) both left all 300 fast tests green (re-confirmed 2026-11-08, unchanged from 2026-11-07), so a wrong interval would ship
Glicko-2 constants (MIN_RD floor 30, system constant TAU) are untested: MIN_RD 30 to 20 and TAU 0.5 to 1.2 both pass all 300 tests

Each respondent's Glicko RD is used as a sampling standard error in a random-effects meta-analysis and the output is labelled a 95% interval, with a normal quantile and as few as 2 to 3 raters per item; the limits are not stated next to the interval
llms.txt points the live page at the retired github.io host instead of https://marisstella.app/quick-pick-survey/ (still unfixed a day after the first audit)
couples.test.ts imports @prisma/client at load, so the 'fast' unit suite cannot load on a fresh checkout until `prisma generate` runs

verdict: Re-audit one day after the first round: scores are identical (correctness 3, completeness 2, verification 2, craft 3, claims 2, fitness 2, domain 2) and it still does not meet the bar. Five new Glicko-2 and DerSimonian-Laird outputs recompute exactly against an independent Python implementation and the typecheck is clean, but the same four seeded changes to the core statistics (1.96 quantile, DL numerator, rating floor, volatility constant) again passed all 300 tests, so the headline 95% interval is right today only because the author was careful. No defect from 2026-11-07 was fixed (fix_prs empty, llms.txt still stale); the only change in the venture was a docs addition, and the suite grew from 298 to 300 tests without covering any of the mutated lines. A methodologist would still object to treating a Glicko RD as a sampling error and to an order-dependent online estimator for a survey. A well-built prototype with no external user, not yet a tool a practitioner would sign off on.
